newsitem.title: MEXICO: PRI chief confident ahead of Mexico elections.
newsitem.headline: PRI chief confident ahead of Mexico elections.

text.p: The national leader of Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) on Monday said he was confident that his party would remain the leading party in Congress after the July 6 mid-term elections.

"At this point it can be said categorically -- and I'm quite aware of where I say it, how I say it and why I say it -- that a majority is practically guranteed," Humberto Roque Villanueva told reporters in this northern industrial city.
"When I say majority, I can't be precise as to whether it will be absolute or (a plurality), but we will be (the largest party), I have no doubt, and you can mark the date I said it," he said.

Mexicans elect all 500 members of the lower house of Congress, one-fourth of the Senate, six state governors and a mayor for Mexico City in a race that political analysts and pollsters say will be a major test for the PRI, which has ruled Mexico since 1929.
Roque said the PRI is leader in polls in the six states that will elect a governo: Colima, San Luis Potosi, Queretaro, Sonora, Campeche and Nuevo Leoon.
